Are you ready to showcase your technical skills, solve real-world problems and compete for exciting career opportunities?

WorkElate presents BuildSprint 2026–28, a solo hiring hackathon designed to identify emerging software engineering talent through technical assessments, problem-solving, screening and an overnight coding challenge.

This is your opportunity to demonstrate your engineering mindset, creativity, technical knowledge and ability to turn ideas into practical solutions.

Compete individually. Win cash prizes. Get considered for internship and full-time career opportunities.

  • Selection Rounds: 4

  • Grand Finale: 18–19 November 2026
  • Final Venue: WorkElate Office, Hyderabad

Eligibility Criteria

Open to candidates pursuing or graduating from:

  • Degrees: B.Tech and BCA
  • Branches: Computer Science, Information Technology and relevant CS specializations.
  • Graduation Years: 2026, 2027 and 2028.

Relevant specializations include AI/ML, Data Science, Cybersecurity and other computing-related disciplines.

Note: Individual participation only. Team registrations are not allowed.

Round 1 – Online Technical Quiz

An online timed quiz to evaluate your technical fundamentals and problem-solving abilities.

Topics may include:

Qualified candidates will receive a problem statement document from WorkElate.

You will have 48 hours (2 days) to understand the problem and submit a proposal explaining your approach and proposed solution.

Important: This round focuses on your proposed solution and approach, not a fully developed application, unless specifically required in the problem statement instructions.

Shortlisted candidates will participate in a screening discussion with the WorkElate team.

The screening will focus on:

  • Technical knowledge and reasoning
  • Problem-solving approach
  • Communication and explanation skills

The best-performing candidates will advance to the final round.

data.title: Rewired (Tech Hackathon)
data.details:
Event Description:

Rewired is a build-and-pitch hackathon. Teams pick a real problem from this year's theme, turn it into a working prototype in 7 hours and pitch it to a jury. It rewards problem sharpness, sound execution, original thinking and the ability to explain why the idea matters to a real user. Coders, designers and business minds are all welcome.

Theme: The Invisible City

Every city runs on things nobody sees: voices no system understands, people who keep everything working but never appear in any database, waste nobody counts, and needs nobody says out loud. Find something real that the city overlooks, and build technology that makes it heard, seen, counted or said.

Event Design:

  • Team size: 2 to 4 members.
  • Eligibility: Open to currently enrolled students from any college or university with a valid college ID. Teams may be cross-college. One person, one team.
  • Equipment: Participants must bring their own laptops, chargers, an extension board and any hardware they use. Power at every desk, Wi-Fi, meals and water are provided at the venue.
  • The Gravity Well: At the start of the Offline Round, each team chooses 1 out of 2 envelopes. It reveals a real-world constraint that the team has to build around. 
  • Tools: Any language, framework, platform, API, library or AI tool may be used, provided it is declared.

Competition Rounds:

Online Round

  • Topic: Restaurants, bakeries, supermarkets and households regularly have surplus food, while people nearby may struggle to afford meals. The challenge is often coordination, timing and safe distribution. Solve this challenge and submit the deliverables listed below for the online round selections. 
    • Challenge: Bridge the gap between those with excess food and those without access to it. 
  • Deliverable: One Concept Brief PDF of up to 2 pages (team, problem with real evidence, target user, proposed solution, tech approach, expected impact, and a 12-hour build plan) and one pitch video of up to 2 minutes in which at least two members appear and speak. 
  • Language: English or Hindi. Videos must have subtitles in English or Hindi.
  • Format: PDF for the brief. .mp4, .mpeg, .avi or .mov for the video.
  • Submission: Upload the brief and video to a Google Drive folder named "Rewired_Team_Name_MWRTMB" set to "Anyone with the link can view", and submit the Drive link, repository link and Orbit on Unstop.
  • Inaccessible link:  If the link cannot be opened at the time of judging, it will be at the discretion of the OC whether the submission will be considered or not.
  • Shortlisting: The Top 20 teams move to the Offline Round.

Offline Round – 19 November 2026

  • Duration: Exactly 7 hours of build time, from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The clock runs through meals and check-ins.
  • Build window: All code, design and assets must be created inside the build window. Push the tags checkpoint-1 by 11:30 AM, checkpoint-2 by 2:30 PM and final by 5:00 PM. GitHub's server push times are the official record.
  • Checkpoints: Each team is assigned one mentor for the day, who holds two check-ins of about 20 minutes during the build. Checkpoints are not scored.
  • Problem Case: A new problem case will be presented to the team at the venue on the day of the offline round. 
  • Submission: Before 5:00 PM, submit the repository link and final commit, a demo link, a mandatory demo video of up to 2 minutes and a completed README through the Google Form provided at the start. Name the Drive folder "REWIRED_TeamID_MWRTMB" and set links to "Anyone with the link can view".
  • Event Horizon Crossing: At 5:00 PM code is frozen. No pushes, Drive changes or redeployments after this point. The recorded final commit is what is judged.
  • Final pitch: All teams pitch to one of four judging panels for 5 minutes, followed by 3 minutes of Q&A. The top teams from each panel go to the Final Orbit and pitch again to the Grand Jury for the top two places.
  • Declarations: Declare all open-source libraries, templates, APIs, datasets and AI tools used, and confirm that the project was built by your team inside the build window through the google form that will be shared at the start.

Rules:

  • Original work: The project must be built by the team inside the build window. Pre-existing projects, old code and borrowed products are not allowed. Open-source libraries, public APIs, templates, UI kits and official project generators are allowed if declared.
  • AI: AI-assisted tools are allowed if declared. Any judge may ask any member to explain any part of the project. If a team cannot explain a core part, its Technical execution score is capped at 10/25.
  • Prototype: Slide-only submissions are not allowed. A working prototype, even a partial one, is required for the Offline Round. If a live demo fails, the team may use its demo video within its pitch time.
  • Team changes: Team members cannot be changed after the Online Round closes. A shortlisted team may replace or drop one member only with written OC approval.
  • Data and IP: Teams must not use confidential or scraped personal data. Teams retain the IP of what they build. Milkyway may feature submissions for promotion with credit to the team. 
  • Pitch time: Pitches over 5 minutes will be cut off by the timekeeper.
  • Conduct: Teams must follow the Code of Conduct and venue rules. Any harassment, sabotage, interference with another team or misuse of the network leads to immediate disqualification.
  • Penalties: All violations will be dealt with under the General Rules, at the discretion of the OC, as set out in the "Penalties and Disqualification" section. Any other consequences will be taken at the discretion of the OC.
  • Any changes to these rules will be informed to the participants prior to the event.

Prizes:

Results will be announced on stage and through mails to all the Participants.

  • 1st place: ₹12,000 and direct entry to the Milkyway Finale.
  • 2nd place: ₹8,000.

Note: Participants shall refer to the General Rules and the Event Horizon Official Participant Rulebook for further details.

Welcome to ZENITH’26, a national-level technical event featuring AWS Student Community Day followed by a 2-Day Hackathon, organized by SCOPE Club, MLRIT, Hyderabad.

Day 1 – AWS Student Community Day

  • Experience a series of high-impact technical workshops and insightful speaker sessions conducted by the AWS Student Builder Group under SCOPE Club, MLRIT.

Day 2 – Hackathon Kickoff

  • The exciting 2-Day Hackathon by SCOPE Club MLRIT begins with team collaboration, ideation, and prototype development.
  • Participants will work on innovative solutions addressing real-world challenges across three domains: AI for Healthcare, AI for Education, and AI for Security.
  • Teams will transform their ideas into functional prototypes using technologies such as AI, ML, Generative AI, and Cloud Computing.
  • Experience an intense development environment filled with creativity, collaboration, and innovation.

Day 3 – Hackathon Finale

  • Teams will refine their prototypes, complete development, and prepare their final presentations.
  • Participants will showcase their solutions before an expert jury panel.
  • Projects will be evaluated based on innovation, technical implementation, feasibility, and real-world impact.
  • The event concludes with the announcement of winners, prize distribution, and a grand closing ceremony celebrating innovation and teamwork.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Team Size: 3–4 members.
  • Participation: Open to college students across India.
  • Team Formation: Inter-college teams are allowed.
  • Preferred Fields: CSE, IT, AI & ML, AI & DS, ECE, and other technical disciplines.

Hackathon Domains

Teams can choose their problem statements from the following domains:

AI for Healthcare

Leveraging AI to improve healthcare accessibility, diagnosis, patient care, medical assistance, and healthcare innovation.

AI for Education

Building intelligent solutions to transform learning experiences, accessibility, personalized education, and educational outcomes.

AI for Security

Developing AI-powered solutions for cybersecurity, surveillance, threat detection, monitoring, and public safety.

  • 18 December 2026: Hackathon Kickoff.
  • 19 December 2026: Hackathon Finale.

Teams incorporating AWS services, AWS tools, or AWS-based architecture into their proposed solutions will have an added advantage during evaluation.

Participants are encouraged to explore how AWS technologies can enhance the scalability, efficiency, reliability, and practical implementation of their ideas. However, using AWS services is not mandatory.

PPT Submission Guidelines:

Shortlisting: Submissions will be evaluated on a rolling basis across all three domains. Shortlisted teams will qualify for Round 2, the on-site hackathon.

- Deadline: 28th Nov’26

The Adaption Dataset Challenge is an online challenge run by Hackyard with Adaption Labs. Every builder gets the same task: improve one dataset using Adaption, then show the before and after on an evaluation agreed with Adaption.

Registration is open now. The challenge task will be announced soon.

Dates

  • Challenge launches and submissions open: Nov 16, 2026

What you get

Register first. Registration is open now and stays open until Dec 6, 2026. The challenge launches and project submissions open on Nov 16. We use the email you register with to issue your Adaption credits, so register with the email you want the credits on.

After you register, sign up at Adaption Labs with the same email you registered with. Adaption whitelists registered emails within one business day of receiving them and sends you one email when your credits are ready.

Improve a dataset for one shared task using Adaption, measure it before and after on an evaluation agreed with Adaption, and show the difference. You submit a project link and a short note on how you used Adaption. The task, the metric and where to submit will be announced.

Judging

Hackyard runs judging. Adaption verifies signups and dataset runs, and a judge from Adaption's team sits on the final round. Judging criteria will be announced.

About

Agentic AI in BFSI: Hackathon 2026 is a national hackathon by Perfios, one of India's largest SaaS TechFin companies serving over 1,000 financial institutions globally, in association with Techfest, IIT Bombay. Under the theme AI Native Applications for BFSI, teams prototype AI-backed systems that can perceive, reason, decide and act across real-world financial workflows. Participants pick one of two banking domains, Debt Collections or Fraud Detection & Prevention, and its problem statement, and are judged on the rigor of their technical plan in Round 1 and on a working prototype at the finals at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia's largest science and technology festival. No prior BFSI experience is needed.

Structure

  • Eligibility: Open to all students with a valid ID from their educational institution. No prior BFSI experience is needed. Cross-institutional teams are encouraged.
  • Team size: Maximum 4 members per team.
  • The competition runs in two rounds, with Round 2 as an in-person prototype demo at Techfest, IIT Bombay.
  • Domains & problems: Teams choose one domain and its problem statement.
    • Theme 1, Debt Collections, has Problem 1: Paralinguistic State Detection from Voice, Not Transcript, where teams build an acoustic model that estimates borrower emotional state (arousal, valence, discrete states, commitment credibility) from speech alone, plus a decision layer that guarantees distressed borrowers are handed to a human and never pressured.
    • Theme 2, Fraud Detection & Prevention, has Problem 2: Know Your Agent (KYA), where teams build a real-time system that detects whether a non-human agent is involved in a banking session, produces an explainable Agent Trust Score, and recommends allow, step-up authentication, hold, or block.

Round 1 - Ideation Round (Online Abstract)

Teams submit a 600-900 word abstract (plus an optional 1-page architecture diagram) covering the problem chosen, understanding of the challenge, proposed approach and agent architecture, how it maps to the Minimum Viable scope, stretch ambitions, expected impact, novelty, evaluation plan, responsible design (fairness, privacy, explainability, safety), and feasibility and risks. No code or prototype is required at this stage; only the Team Leader may submit, and multiple submissions are not accepted. Perfios evaluates submissions and shortlists the most promising ideas based on creativity, feasibility, and relevance.

Round 2 - Prototype & Demo (Finals)

Shortlisted teams build a working prototype covering the Minimum Viable scope of their problem (and any stretch goals attempted) and present it at IIT Bombay to a panel of Perfios judges. Each team gets 20 minutes for presentation and live demo, followed by 5 minutes of Q&A. Finalists submit a code repository with README, a technical report (max 6 pages), a results summary table against every success metric, and a demo video (max 3 minutes) as a backup. Winners are selected on innovation, technical depth, prototype quality, and real-world applicability.

Timeline

  • Submission link opens - 15th November 2026
  • Registration closes - 25th November 2026
  • Round 1 submission deadline - 30th November 2026
  • Shortlist announcement - 4th December 2026
  • Finals at IIT Bombay - 15th-18th December 2026

Rewards And Prizes

  • INR 1,00,000 for the top 3 winners.
  • Certificates for all participants who qualify for Round 2.

BUILD. INNOVATE. ENGINEER THE FUTURE.

OVERCLOCK 2027 is a 24-hour national-level hardware hackathon organized by the Department of Electrical Engineering, Fr. C. Rodrigues Institute of Technology (FCRIT), Vashi, Navi Mumbai, in association with IEEE FCRIT Student Branch (STB 61121), EESA and ISLE FCRIT.

  • 15 December 2026: Round 1 Submission Deadline (11:59 PM IST)
  • 22 December 2026: Shortlist Announcement (Top 30 Teams + 5 Waitlisted)
  • 22 January 2027: Finale Problem Statements Released

Round 1 – Online Proposal Screening

100% Free – No Registration Fee

  • Register your team and select a problem statement.
  • Submit your proposed solution using the official PPT template.
  • Explain your problem understanding, proposed approach, hardware architecture, components and technical feasibility.
  • No physical prototype is required during this round.
  • All teams can participate in Round 1 without any payment.

Round 2 – 24-Hour On-Campus Finale

₹1,500 + 18% GST = ₹1,770 PER TEAM

  • Only shortlisted teams will be required to pay the Round 2 participation fee.
  • Finalists will receive fresh problem statements one week before the event.
  • Teams will design, assemble, program and demonstrate a functional hardware prototype within 24 hours.
  • All final assembly, soldering, wiring and firmware development must take place during the event. Completed prototypes and pre-assembled final circuits are not permitted.

Payment Information: Round 2 participation fees will be collected separately through the official FCRIT institutional payment portal after shortlisting and confirmation. No payment is required through Unstop for Round 1 registration or submission.

  • Energy, Power & Sustainability – Renewable energy, smart grids, EV technology, power management and energy efficiency.
  • Smart Home & Consumer Electronics – Smart appliances, household safety, IoT and consumer-focused hardware.
  • Industrial Automation & Monitoring – Industrial sensors, predictive maintenance, fault detection and automation.
  • Defence & National Security – Field equipment, surveillance, remote monitoring, communication and personnel safety.
  • Healthcare & Assistive Technology – Patient monitoring, rehabilitation, medical equipment and assistive devices.

  • Access to selected college laboratory equipment and workshop facilities, subject to availability and safety protocols.

Overview

Get ready for the Remote Robotics (ReRo) Online Hackathon at PES University, organized by the IEEE Robotics and Automation Society (IEEE RAS) Chapter, RR Campus, PES University!

A national-level, fully online hackathon and a flagship event of IEEE RAS. Open to all students across the country. Code real robots, test them on real tracks, and compete from anywhere!

Introducing ReRo Lab

The ReRo Lab, inaugurated in February 2023 at PES University, stands as India’s first-ever 24/7 remote robotics facility built by an educational institution. It’s not just a lab, it’s a space where innovation literally never sleeps. From programming mobile robots in real time to testing algorithms and collaborating with peers across the globe, ReRo lets you experience the future of robotics from any part of the world, remotely. Whether you're just starting out or already deep into robotics, this is where curiosity meets cutting-edge.

Mode

Virtual (via ReRo Lab Platform)

Why Participate?

  • Access real robots at a world-class facility without stepping into the lab
  • Build your own algorithm from scratch and test it on real tracks
  • Sharpen your programming, control (PID) and problem-solving skills
  • Compete at a national level and win cash prizes

How It Works

  • Round 1 (Friday, 13th November): Online quiz on PID and robotics fundamentals. Top teams move ahead.
  • Round 2 (Sat-Sun, 14th-15th November): 24-hour remote hackathon. Code your own algorithm and run it on our bots in two arenas: Line Follower and Maze Solver (More information on this will be given later).
  • Bot access: 3 slots of 20 minutes per team, booked on the ReRo Lab website (first-come, first-serve basis).

Event Details

  • Open to: All students across India
  • Team Size: 1-3
  • Venue: Virtual, remote access via our web platform

Prizes

  • Total cash prize pool of ₹7,000
  • Individual IEEE memberships for the winning students

data.details:
VYOM Edition 1 (2026–27) — Official Event Overview & Guidelines

VYOM Edition 1 (2026–27) is a premier National-Level Hardware + Software Hackathon cum Project Expo organized by the Government College of Engineering, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (GECCS) in association with the Center of Excellence (CoE) – TSSIP and the Ankur Incubation Center Foundation (AICF).

Event at a Glance & Key Details

  • Dates: 2–3 January 2027 (Saturday–Sunday)
  • Venue: Government College of Engineering, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (GECCS Campus)
  • Total Prize Pool: ₹50,000+ (with separate prizes for Hardware and Software tracks)
  • Organized By: Government College of Engineering, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (GECCS)
  • In Association With: Center of Excellence (CoE) – TSSIP & Ankur Incubation Center Foundation (AICF)
  • Supporters: HackSlash, C-Cube, and Cybrotics

Team Eligibility & Formation Guidelines

  • Eligible Participants: Open to all undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma, and B.Sc. students enrolled in any recognized institute or university across India.
  • Team Size: 3 to 5 members per team, including a designated Team Leader. Individual participation is not permitted.
  • Cross-College & Multidisciplinary Teams: Inter-college and multidisciplinary/inter-specialization teams (combining different engineering branches and academic years) are strongly encouraged and fully permitted.

️ Innovation Domains (10 Tracks)

Teams can participate in either the Hardware Track or the Software Track across 10 specialized domains, or opt for dual participation:

Hardware Innovation Track (5 Domains)

  1. Robotics, Automation & Drone Technology: Unmanned aerial systems, intelligent robotics, automated guided vehicles (AGVs), and kinematics.
  2. Smart Sensors, IoT & Wearable Technology: Connected edge devices, smart telemetry, biometric wearables, and distributed sensor grids.
  3. Renewable Energy & Smart Power Systems: Battery management systems (BMS), microgrid optimization, green generation, and load automation.
  4. Industrial Automation & Smart Manufacturing: Industry 4.0, PLC interfacing, process monitoring, and predictive maintenance.
  5. Open Innovation Track (Hardware): Original hardware ideas beyond the listed domains, including novel devices, prototypes, and engineering solutions.

Software Innovation Track (5 Domains)

  1. Healthcare & MedTech: Digital health registries, assistive clinical tools, and diagnostic data processing.
  2. AI, ML & Computational Intelligence: Neural architectures, computer vision, NLP, and predictive models.
  3. Agriculture & Smart Farming: Precision agronomy, soil monitoring, and yield prediction.
  4. Social Innovation & Rural Development: Community empowerment, rural utility access, and digital inclusion.
  5. Open Innovation Track (Software): Novel technologies, cybersecurity, fintech, and next-gen cloud/web platforms.

Competition Process & Format

The event follows a structured 3-round format:

  • Round 1: PPT / Idea Submission (Online)

    • Registration Fee: 100% Free.
    • Format: Participants submit a structured PowerPoint presentation under either the Hardware or Software category.
    • Presentation Guidelines: Exactly 7 slides are required. Slide 1 must include basic team details, the team leader's name, the chosen problem statement, track, and domain. All slides must display the team's official logo. No rigid design template is mandated.
  • Round 2: Online Screening & Mentorship

    • Registration Fee: 100% Free.
    • Format: Submitted proposals and PPTs are evaluated by domain experts. Shortlisted teams qualify for the final round.
  • Round 3: On-Campus Grand Finale — 12-Hour Offline Hackathon & Project Expo

    • Venue: GECCS Campus, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
    • Registration Fee: ₹999 per selected team (applicable only to teams selected for Round 3; includes dinner and refreshments).
    • Format: Intensive 12-hour offline hackathon sprint where teams develop, integrate, and present their working solutions and live prototypes. Software teams require a fully working app or website live for demo, while Hardware teams must showcase a working prototype.

Key Rules & Policies

  • Dual Participation: Teams are permitted to participate in both Software and Hardware tracks simultaneously, provided their chosen problem statements and solutions are entirely distinct.
  • AI & Development Tools: The use of AI software and coding assistants (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, etc.) is fully permitted for development, debugging, and ideation across all stages.
  • Open Innovation Policy: Pre-existing projects are welcomed under Open Innovation, provided teams explicitly highlight pre-existing components during evaluation and demonstrate newly added value or extensions built during the hackathon timeline.
  • Intellectual Property (IP): Participating student teams retain full ownership and intellectual property rights over their codebases, designs, and prototypes, with fast-track pre-incubation support opportunities through AICF and CoE – TSSIP.

  • Director General (VYOM): Vedant Rani Shankar Jha – [phone]- [email]
  • Official Support Email: [email]
  • Registration Portal: Register via the official Unstop platform or Google Form links provided in the official portal.

data.details:
VibeForge – National-Level Hackathon | NIMS Quest 1.0

VibeForge is a national-level hackathon organised by the STEM Department, NIMS University Rajasthan, as part of NIMS Quest 1.0.

The hackathon challenges participants to transform innovative ideas into functional prototypes within a three-hour time limit. By combining programming, AI-assisted development tools, and modern coding workflows, participants will develop practical, technology-driven solutions to real-world problems.

The competition encourages creativity, innovation, technical execution, and effective problem-solving. Participants must demonstrate their ability to develop a working prototype, explain their technical approach, and communicate the real-world applications of their solutions.

Competition Details

Date: 25 November 2026
Time: 9:30 AM – 12:30 PM IST
Duration: 3 hours
Format: Team-based hackathon
Competition Level: National
Organiser: STEM Department, NIMS University Rajasthan
Total Prize Pool: ₹15,000

Eligibility Criteria

The hackathon is open to all the undergraduate students or students from colleges and universities across India. Participants must register through the official Unstop listing within the registration period and meet the eligibility requirements established by the organising committee.

Team Size: 1-4

Each team must register its members according to the instructions provided by the organisers.

Competition Format and Process

The hackathon will consist of three evaluation stages conducted within the allotted three-hour duration.

Teams will identify a problem, develop an innovative solution, build a functional prototype using programming and AI tools, and present their solution through a final pitch and live demonstration within three hours.

Mode: Offline

Rules and Guidelines

  1. Participants must complete registration and provide accurate information as required by the organisers.
  2. Teams must comply with the announced eligibility criteria and team-size requirements.
  3. All development and submissions must be completed within the allotted competition duration.
  4. Participants must submit original work and must not plagiarise or present another team's work as their own.
  5. AI-assisted coding tools and other development resources may be used in accordance with the guidelines announced by the organisers.
  6. Teams must be able to explain their solution, implementation, and use of development tools during evaluation.
  7. Participants must follow all submission instructions and deadlines communicated by the organising committee.
  8. Any attempt to manipulate the evaluation process, misrepresent work, or gain an unfair advantage may result in disqualification.
  9. The organising committee's decisions regarding competition administration and disqualification will be final.

Evaluation Criteria

Innovation and Originality: 20%
Functionality and Execution: 25%
Problem Relevance: 15%
AI and Modern Tool Integration: 15%
UI/UX Design: 10%
Presentation and Pitch: 10%
Time Management: 5%

The total evaluation weightage is 100%. Judges will assess submissions based on the published criteria, the functionality of the prototype, and the team's ability to explain its solution.

Prizes and Recognition

VibeForge offers a total prize pool of ₹15,000.

First Prize: ₹7,000
Second Prize: ₹5,000
Third Prize: ₹3,000

Certificates and additional recognition: To all the winners and participants.

Prize distribution will be subject to verification of the winners and the conditions announced by the organising committee.

VibeForge welcomes aspiring developers, innovators, and technology enthusiasts to collaborate, build functional prototypes, and present creative solutions to real-world challenges. Join the challenge to showcase your technical skills, transform ideas into working solutions, and compete for exciting rewards at NIMS Quest 1.0.
